name: Paracetamol
indications: Fever, mild to moderate pain, headache, body ache, toothache, post-vaccination fever
dosage: Adults: 500-650mg per dose every 4-6 hours as needed. Maximum 4 doses per day (max 3g per day). Children: 10-15mg per kg per dose every 4-6 hours.
side_effects: Rare at normal doses. Overdose causes serious liver damage. Do not exceed recommended dose.
contraindications: Liver disease, chronic alcohol use. Do not combine with other paracetamol-containing products.

name: Cetirizine
indications: Allergic rhinitis, urticaria (hives), allergic skin reactions, itching, runny nose due to allergy
dosage: Adults and children above 12 years: 10mg once daily at bedtime. Children 6-12 years: 5mg twice daily.
side_effects: Mild drowsiness (less than older antihistamines), dry mouth, fatigue. Avoid driving if drowsy.
contraindications: Kidney disease (reduce dose). Caution with alcohol and sedatives.

name: ORS (Oral Rehydration Salts)
indications: Dehydration from diarrhoea, vomiting, heat exhaustion, fever with fluid loss, cholera
dosage: Dissolve 1 sachet in 1 litre clean boiled cooled water. Adults: 200-400ml after each loose stool. Children: 50-100ml per kg body weight over 3-4 hours for moderate dehydration.
side_effects: Safe at correct dilution. Nausea if taken too quickly. Do not dilute more or less than instructed.
contraindications: Severe dehydration with vomiting (IV fluids needed). Kidney failure.

name: Pantoprazole
indications: Acidity, GERD (gastroesophageal reflux), peptic ulcer disease, stomach pain from excess acid
dosage: Adults: 40mg once daily 30 minutes before breakfast. Course: 4-8 weeks for GERD, up to 8 weeks for ulcers.
side_effects: Headache, diarrhoea, nausea, abdominal pain. Long-term use (above 1 year) may reduce magnesium and Vitamin B12.
contraindications: Severe liver disease. Do not use long-term without medical supervision. Do not combine with Clopidogrel.

name: Ibuprofen
indications: Fever, mild to moderate pain, inflammation, arthritis, menstrual cramps, dental pain, musculoskeletal pain
dosage: Adults: 200-400mg every 6-8 hours with food. Maximum 1200mg per day for OTC use. Always take with food or milk to protect stomach.
side_effects: Stomach irritation, gastric ulcers with prolonged use, increased bleeding risk, kidney effects with dehydration, fluid retention.
contraindications: CRITICAL: DO NOT USE IN DENGUE FEVER as it dramatically increases bleeding risk. Avoid with stomach ulcers, kidney disease, heart failure, dehydration. Avoid in last trimester of pregnancy. Caution in elderly patients.

name: Digene Gel
brand_names: Digene Gel, Gelusil MPS, Mucaine Gel, Eno (powder)
indications: Acidity, heartburn, bloating, indigestion, gas, sour stomach
dosage: Adults: 10-20ml gel or 1-2 tablets after meals and at bedtime. Maximum 4 doses per day. Take at least 2 hours away from other medications.
side_effects: Constipation (aluminium-containing antacids), diarrhoea (magnesium-containing). Avoid long-term use.
contraindications: Kidney disease. Do not take within 2 hours of other medications as it reduces their absorption.

name: Loperamide
indications: Acute non-infectious diarrhoea, traveller's diarrhoea, chronic diarrhoea
dosage: Adults: 4mg initial dose then 2mg after each loose stool. Maximum 16mg per day. Do not use for more than 2 days without medical advice.
contraindications: Do NOT use in bloody diarrhoea, dysentery, or high fever (may worsen bacterial infection). Do not use in children below 2 years. Do not use if diarrhoea is caused by antibiotics (C. diff).

name: Azithromycin
indications: Community-acquired pneumonia, typhoid fever, pharyngitis, skin infections, chlamydia
dosage: Adults: 500mg once daily for 3-5 days depending on infection. Must complete full course even if feeling better.
side_effects: Nausea, diarrhoea, abdominal discomfort, mild liver enzyme elevation. Rare: QT prolongation (cardiac risk).
contraindications: Severe liver disease, heart rhythm abnormalities (Long QT syndrome). PRESCRIPTION REQUIRED. Never self-medicate antibiotics.

name: Amoxicillin
indications: Respiratory tract infections, ear infections (otitis media), urinary tract infections, H. pylori eradication (with other drugs)
dosage: Adults: 250-500mg three times daily for 5-7 days. Children: 25-50mg per kg per day in divided doses.
side_effects: Diarrhoea, nausea, rash, allergic reactions. Up to 10% of people allergic to penicillin.
contraindications: Penicillin allergy (serious risk of anaphylaxis). PRESCRIPTION REQUIRED.

name: Metformin
indications: Type 2 diabetes management. First-line drug for most patients.
dosage: Starting dose: 500mg twice daily with meals. Increased gradually to 1000-2000mg per day in divided doses. Take with food to reduce GI side effects.
side_effects: Nausea, diarrhoea, metallic taste (usually resolves after 2-3 weeks). Very rarely: lactic acidosis (serious).
contraindications: Kidney disease (eGFR below 30 ml/min), liver disease, heart failure, before contrast dye procedures (stop 48 hours before). PRESCRIPTION REQUIRED.

name: Amlodipine
indications: Hypertension (high blood pressure), angina (chest pain from heart disease)
dosage: Adults: 5mg once daily. May increase to 10mg if needed. Take at the same time each day.
side_effects: Ankle swelling (pedal oedema), flushing, headache, dizziness, palpitations.
contraindications: Severe low blood pressure, aortic stenosis. PRESCRIPTION REQUIRED. Do not stop suddenly.

name: Salbutamol Inhaler
indications: Acute asthma attack, wheezing, bronchospasm, exercise-induced asthma, COPD
dosage: Acute attack: 2 puffs (200 mcg) every 4-6 hours as needed. Use spacer device if available especially for children. Maximum 8 puffs per day without medical review.
side_effects: Tremors (shaking hands), rapid heartbeat (palpitations), headache, nervousness. These are dose-related and usually mild.
contraindications: Heart disease (use with caution). Overuse reduces effectiveness. PRESCRIPTION REQUIRED for initial prescription but commonly available.

name: Ondansetron
indications: Nausea and vomiting from gastroenteritis, chemotherapy, post-surgery, pregnancy (severe morning sickness)
dosage: Adults: 4-8mg up to 3 times daily. Children above 4 years: 0.1-0.15mg per kg per dose (max 4mg). Oral disintegrating tablet dissolves on tongue without water.
side_effects: Headache, constipation, dizziness, warm flushing feeling.
contraindications: Long QT syndrome, severe liver disease, congenital heart defects. PRESCRIPTION REQUIRED.

name: Vitamin C (Ascorbic Acid)
indications: Vitamin C deficiency, to enhance iron absorption, immunity support, wound healing
dosage: Adults: 500-1000mg daily. For iron absorption: take with iron supplements or iron-rich meals. Safe up to 2000mg per day.
side_effects: High doses (above 2000mg) may cause diarrhoea, kidney stones in susceptible individuals.
contraindications: Kidney stones history (limit to 200mg daily), G6PD deficiency (haemolytic anaemia risk with very high doses).

name: Zinc Sulphate
brand_names: Zincovit, Zinco, Z and D, Zinconia
indications: Zinc deficiency, diarrhoea treatment in children (WHO recommendation), wound healing, immune support
dosage: Diarrhoea in children: 20mg per day for 14 days (10mg per day for children below 6 months). Adults supplementation: 10-25mg per day with food.
side_effects: Nausea and vomiting if taken on empty stomach. High doses interfere with copper absorption.
contraindications: Do not take on empty stomach. Avoid high doses long-term without medical advice.
